hooks.text: At 430,000 miles per hour, NASA's fastest craft dives into the Sun.
A carbon shield keeps this solar probe cool while diving into hell.
It plunges through solar fire without melting, becoming history's fastest craft.

title: The Fastest Craft Ever Built Plunges Into the Sun
description: Discover how NASA's Parker Solar Probe survives extreme temperatures while becoming the fastest human-made object in history.

beats.text: At 430,000 miles per hour, NASA's fastest craft dives into the Sun.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Parker Solar Probe approaching the Sun, NASA, 2018

beats.text: Launched in 2018, this mission honors the pioneering astrophysicist Eugene Newman Parker.
beats.visual: Photograph of astrophysicist Eugene Parker, University of Chicago, 2005

beats.text: The project cost approximately 1.5 billion dollars and required extreme engineering to complete the journey.
beats.visual: Delta IV Heavy rocket launch carrying the Parker Solar Probe, NASA, 2018
queries: Delta IV Heavy launch Parker Solar Probe

beats.text: To reach the blistering outer atmosphere, the probe executes seven Venus gravity assists over seven long years.
beats.visual: NASA spacecraft illustration of a Venus gravity assist maneuver, 2018

beats.text: A massive 4.5-inch-thick carbon-composite heat shield protects the four sensitive instrument suites tucked deep inside.
beats.visual: Diagram of the Parker Solar Probe heat shield layers, NASA, 2018
queries: Parker Solar Probe heat shield diagram

beats.text: While the exterior withstands temperatures reaching nearly 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, sensitive internal electronics stay at a constant 85 degrees.
beats.visual: Solar corona and coronal mass ejection captured by SOHO telescope, NASA, 2012

beats.text: That brilliant engineering finally lets humanity directly touch our star at 430,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the Parker Solar Probe diving through the solar corona, NASA, 2018
queries: Parker Solar Probe spacecraft artist illustration
